title: What If the Suez Canal Closed for a Week?

scenes.text: What if the Suez Canal closed for a week? It already did, and the bill was billions.
In 2021, the container ship Ever Given wedged sideways in the canal and blocked it for six days.
Around twelve percent of global trade passes through Suez. Lloyd's List estimated about nine point six billion dollars of goods held up each day.
Allianz estimated six to ten billion dollars of added costs for every week the ship stayed stuck.
Dredgers and tugboats worked for days to free it, and even afterwards, delays rippled through shipping.
One ship, one canal, six days. That is how thin world trade's margin can be.
